summary: Weekly POC sync. Reviewed quality evaluation results across prompt sets; identified a small regression in discharge-summary prompts after guardrail tightening. Agreed on prompt tweaks, scoring threshold adjustments, and a follow-up regression run. Security asked for SOC2 appendix and KMS flow; SE to provide more detailed token-level traces for failing examples. Planning a cost/latency benchmark on dedicated config week of 2026-04-20.
questions: How severe is the regression in discharge-summary prompts?
Can we keep latency SLOs while adding guardrails?
Will dedicated reduce unit cost for our workload?
How does Redwood handle KMS keys for private deployments?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Marco Liu (Redwood CSM), Dr. Maya Patel (Lumen - Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Lumen - Eng Lead), Priya Nair (Lumen - Security)

[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Thursday. Quick check — does everyone have the eval spreadsheet link? I posted in chat.
[00:18] Dr. Maya Patel: Yep I have it, opening now. Sorry running a bit behind this morning.
[00:25] Priya Shah: No worries, we'll go over the high level first then dive into the failing set. So the key updates from last week: we tightened the guardrails on the discharge-summary prompt and raised the hallucination threshold per your feedback. We re-ran the test suite against the 5k prompt set.
[00:45] Ethan Cole: Quick clarification, by "tightened guardrails" do you mean additional system role constraints or a hard filter after generation?
[01:02] Priya Shah: Good question. It's a mix — we strengthened system instructions plus added a post-run heuristic that flags potential PHI leakage and drops risky completions. It's not perfect, we saw some effect on quality.
[01:20] Dr. Maya Patel: Right, and the headline for us is we saw about a 4.3% drop in ROUGE-L on discharge-summary prompts, which is our main concern. Other templates stayed largely stable.
[01:40] Alex Rivera: I pulled the chart here — overall pass rate is 92% but discharge-summary fell from 96 to 91.7. There's a cluster of examples where the model omits medication changes, likely the guardrail filter being overzealous.
[02:05] Ethan Cole: Is that the KV cache thing? Last time Priya mentioned K-V cache causing some token truncation in streaming.
[02:18] Priya Shah: That's probably a transcription artifact — it's KV cache. But this isn't a cache bug; it's the post-filter removing sentences that mention meds because of pattern matching for PHI. The regex is a bit aggressive.
[02:36] Dr. Maya Patel: Hmm, that makes sense. We definitely can't lose med change info. That's a clinical risk for us.
[02:48] Priya Nair: From security perspective, the filter is necessary but we need more granular controls — ability to whitelist entities or allow structured redaction instead of blunt removal.
[03:05] Priya Shah: Agreed. On staging I can add entity-aware masking instead of dropping whole sentences. That should preserve the med changes but redact identifiers.
[03:20] Alex Rivera: Also on scoring, we compared the old threshold with a slightly relaxed one; if we relax the hallucination flag from 0.6 to 0.7 we regain about 2% ROUGE but with a small uptick in risky tokens. So tradeoff.
[03:40] Dr. Maya Patel: Can you show an example?
[03:50] Priya Shah: Yeah, example ID 4821 in the sheet — original expected answer lists med change to metformin, the guarded completion redacted the word and left a sentence fragment "... dosage adjusted to [REDACTED]". That counts as omission in the scoring.
[04:18] Ethan Cole: Ok so engineering ask — can we preserve semantics while redacting PHI? Like "medication: [type: metformin, dose: 500mg]" structure vs just removing.
[04:34] Priya Shah: We can try structured placeholders, or we can move to a named-entity-aware mask that preserves drug names but strips patient identifiers. We'll need to tune NER thresholds.
[04:50] Marco Liu: From the CSM side, we want to prioritize the user's acceptance criteria — you mentioned in the doc that med-change accuracy must stay above 95% for go/no-go, right Maya?
[05:05] Dr. Maya Patel: Correct, med-change and allergy mentions are critical.
[05:12] Alex Rivera: Ok, let's put that in the action items.
[05:20] Priya Nair: On encryption — quick question — does Redwood use customer-managed KMS for private deployments? Our security team needs details for audit.
[05:32] Priya Shah: Yes, for Private (VPC) we support customer KMS/HSM, keys never leave your control. For hosted, we can do bring-your-own-key for certain tiers. We'll attach the SOC2 appendix and the KMS flow diagram in the follow-up.
[05:52] Priya Nair: Great, please include the key rotation policy and separation of duties.
[06:00] Alex Rivera: Will do.
[06:05] Dr. Maya Patel: Back to regressions — do you have a list of the top failing prompts so we can triage?
[06:12] Priya Shah: Yes, sheet tab "Failing_20260408" — about 120 failures flagged, but top 25 are reproducible across seeds. I've highlighted 8 that are med-change omissions.
[06:28] Ethan Cole: I'm seeing a couple that look like hallucinations too — invented follow-up appointment times. Were those introduced by the model change or the guardrail?
[06:42] Priya Shah: Those were model behavior; we didn't touch the generation model itself, but the guardrail can exacerbate fragmentation which sometimes causes the model to invent a short plausible time.
[06:56] Dr. Maya Patel: So two parallel tracks: reduce hallucination and fix PHI masking.
[07:04] Priya Shah: Exactly. Proposed approach: 1) change masking to entity-aware redaction on staging, 2) adjust hallucination threshold and score weighting to favor recall for med-change, 3) re-run nightly regression with token-level logging.
[07:22] Alex Rivera: For the regression run — can you run it with the new prompts and send the raw traces? We'll need token-level logs for the 25 worst cases.
[07:33] Priya Shah: Yes, token-level logs can be enabled for staging; we'll obfuscate patient identifiers from logs before sending.
[07:44] Marco Liu: On scheduling the benchmark — once we have the guardrail change, we should do a dedicated run to measure latency impact. Ethan, do you have a preference for dedicated vs hosted for the benchmark?
[07:58] Ethan Cole: We'd like to see both. Our cost model assumes we'll move to Dedicated if unit cost drops 20% at our volume. So a side-by-side would be ideal.
[08:12] Priya Shah: We can schedule a dedicated pool run; I estimate we'll need 2 hours of steady-state load to get stable numbers. We'll capture p50/p90 latencies and per-token cost estimates.
[08:25] Dr. Maya Patel: Perfect. Also one more question — in the last meeting you mentioned continuous caching, does Redwood persist kv cache across requests for the same patient session? We worry about cross-session leakage.
[08:40] Priya Shah: By default caches are session-isolated. For dedicated you can set longer KV cache TTLs but they remain tenant-scoped. We can send the cache isolation docs.
[08:52] Alex Rivera: I'll add links in the follow-up.
[08:58] Ethan Cole: Something else — on scoring metrics, can you include precision/recall and a human judgement column? Automated metrics are noisy for clinical text.
[09:12] Priya Shah: Yes we've added a human-eval column for a 200-sample subset. We can expand that if you want.
[09:22] Dr. Maya Patel: Please do 500 if possible — it's more robust for safety signals.
[09:29] Marco Liu: We'll scope it, but note that'll add time to labeling.
[09:35] Priya Shah: Understood. We'll propose a plan in the follow-up.
[09:42] Alex Rivera: Any competitors or other platforms you're considering that might change the POC priorities?
[09:49] Dr. Maya Patel: We're evaluating Anthropic for safety features but cost is a concern; OpenAI is still on the table for a hosted-only approach. You folks are strongest on deployment flexibility which matters.
[10:03] Alex Rivera: Got it.
[10:06] Priya Nair: Security wrap — please include RBAC details, audit log sample, and how SSO/SAML integrates.
[10:14] Priya Shah: We'll attach the security pack.
[10:18] Alex Rivera: Ok let's recap next steps: Alex will send updated eval spreadsheet + prompt diffs; Priya (SE) will deploy entity-aware masking on staging and enable token traces; Maya will provide 25 failing examples; Priya Nair will send KMS/audit questions; Marco will schedule the benchmark.
[10:40] Dr. Maya Patel: Sounds good. Thank you.
[10:44] Ethan Cole: Thanks team.
[10:46] Priya Shah: Quick note — for the entity-aware masking we'll trial two variants: preserve drug names vs preserve drug classes. We'll include both in the re-run.
[10:56] Alex Rivera: Great. We'll reconvene same time next week; if the regression is fixed we can move to scale validation.
[11:05] Meeting end.

Notes on artifacts: "Eval spreadsheet" link: https://redwood.example.com/evals/Lumen-2026-04-08 (shared in chat). SOC2 appendix & KMS flow: will be attached in follow-up email.

Transcription notes: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KV cache transcribed sometimes as K V cash), names sometimes mismatched in auto transcription.
